title: Algorithms, Complexity, and Entropy of the Bernard-Letac Fair-Sampling Construction
summary: Bernard and Letac (1971) introduced a method for uniform random sampling among $m$ outcomes from an unknown biased source of independent and identically distributed symbols. The process terminates when the multinomial coefficient of the cumulative symbol counts equals zero modulo $m$. This study extends the computational and information-theoretic analysis of their construction by presenting five algorithms with formal correctness guarantees and comprehensive complexity analyses.
